The bug is in two places. `billing.AddInterval` clamps nothing, and `renew` takes the next period's start from the run time (`now`), not from the previous period's end. The fix goes in `billing` as an anchor-based `PeriodStart`, and `renew` loops over every period that has started. Before editing, here is the definition of done:

Definition of done:
- Period boundaries are computed from the anchor (`StartedAt`, or `TrialEnd` for trials) and never drift after short months: Jan 31 → Feb 28 → Mar 31, and a Feb 29 yearly anchor gives Feb 28 / Feb 29 as specified.
- `RenewDue` renews every period that has started by now, in order, each with its own invoice, so a job that runs two months late produces the same periods as one that runs on time.
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass, with new tests in `internal/billing` and `internal/subscriptions` covering the month-end, leap-year, catch-up and metered cases.

Definition of done:
- Period boundaries come from the anchor (`StartedAt`, or `TrialEnd` for trials), so they no longer drift after short months. Jan 31 gives Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, and a Feb 29 yearly anchor gives Feb 28 / Feb 29.
- `RenewDue` renews every period that has started by now, in order, each with its own invoice, so a job that runs two months late produces the same periods as one that runs on time.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass, with new tests in `internal/billing` and `internal/subscriptions` covering month-end, leap-year, catch-up and metered cases.

The fix is in place and all three checks pass. Nothing is committed.

**Changes**
- `internal/billing/billing.go`
  - `AddInterval` now clamps to the last day of a short month. Its signature is unchanged.
  - New `PeriodStart(anchor, iv, n)` computes period n from the anchor, in UTC.
  - New `PeriodIndex(anchor, iv, t)` returns the first period that starts at or after `t`.
- `internal/subscriptions/subscriptions.go`
  - New `anchor(sub)` helper: `TrialEnd` if set, otherwise `StartedAt`.
  - `renew` starts at the period index of `CurrentPeriodEnd` and renews each period whose start is not after `now`, saving each one as it goes. Each period gets its own invoice.
  - Metered plans bill the period that ended, once per ended period, and skip the trial period.
  - `RenewDue` counts a subscription only when it actually renewed or canceled it.
- `internal/billing/billing_test.go`: tests for the anchor-day rule, the leap-day yearly anchor, the clamped `AddInterval`, and `PeriodIndex`.
- `internal/subscriptions/subscriptions_test.go`
  - Month-end renewal: Jan 31, then Feb 28, then Mar 31.
  - Late job: a run on May 1 renews three missed periods, giving three invoices and charges. A second run renews nothing.
  - Metered catch-up: two ended periods give two invoices with their own usage.
  - `TestTrialThenRenewal` had its expectation changed. It asserted the old drifting end date (Mar 1 after a Jan 29 trial). The correct end is now Feb 28, so I updated that assertion.

**Choices I made that you may want to review**
- If a charge is declined partway through a catch-up, the rest of the periods are still renewed and invoiced. The subscription ends the run `past_due` if any period was declined. Stopping early would leave the declined period to be invoiced again on the next run.
- Subscriptions whose stored period end has already drifted (for example, `Mar 3` from the old bug) renew from the first correct boundary at or after that date. This can leave a gap for those rows, and I did not write a migration for existing data.

The change meets the task text and the worker's definition of done. I read the diff against the code paths it touches (`Create`, `DueSubscriptions`, `RenewDue`, `renew`) and traced the new tests by hand. I did not re-run the tools, since the evidence already covers build, test and lint.

Checks that hold:
- **Month-end and leap-year math:** `PeriodStart` counts from the anchor and clamps the day to the target month's length. Jan 31 gives Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30. A Feb 29 yearly anchor gives Feb 28 in common years and Feb 29 in leap years.
- **Catch-up:** `PeriodIndex` finds the period that starts at `CurrentPeriodEnd`, and the loop renews each period whose start is not after `now`. For a subscription created Jan 31 and run May 1, this produces the same Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30 periods as an on-time job.
- **Metered:** each renewed period bills the period that just ended, using `prevStart`/`prevEnd`. In the trial-then-metered case, the first iteration skips billing because the status is still Trialing, and the next iteration bills the first paid period. That matches the old behaviour.
- **Store contract:** `DueSubscriptions` selects subscriptions whose `CurrentPeriodEnd` is not after `now`, so `renew` always starts from an ended period.

Non-blocking notes:
- **Legacy data (`internal/subscriptions/subscriptions.go`, around line 199):** a subscription already drifted by the old code, with `CurrentPeriodEnd` on, say, Mar 3, will be renewed from the next anchored start (Mar 31). The Mar 3 to Mar 31 span is then never invoiced. The task does not mention a migration, so this is optional to address; a one-off data fix or a note in the change would cover it.
- **Coverage (`internal/subscriptions/subscriptions_test.go`):** the leap-year case is tested only at the `billing` level. The subscriptions tests cover month-end, catch-up and metered. A yearly or leap-year renewal test would match the definition of done more literally.
- **Decline behaviour:** after one declined period, later catch-up periods are still invoiced and charged. The subscription ends up past due, which is reasonable, but it is a choice worth confirming.

{"verdict":"SHIP","feedback":""}
